reasoning: Idaho remains a deeply Republican state, with its statewide Cook Partisan Voting Index at R+28. In the last 45 days, the most directly relevant general-election information for the 2026 Senate race shows Jim Risch ahead by roughly 40 points in a June statewide poll, while forecast/odds pages and news coverage consistently characterize the race as strongly Republican and generally in the mid-30s to 40-point GOP range.

sources.name: PredictionHunt citing Peak Insights
sources.details: A June 2026 statewide poll found Jim Risch at 55%, Democratic nominee David Roth at 15%, and smaller shares for independents and a Libertarian, implying a very large Republican lead.

sources.name: PollsMax Idaho Senate Forecast
sources.details: A polling-average/forecast page for Idaho's 2026 Senate race shows a projected Republican margin of about 36 points and notes only one general-election poll in the average.

sources.name: The Downballot citing Bullfinch Group
sources.details: Coverage summarizing an early June Bullfinch Group poll said Risch led Achilles 40-36 in a hypothetical one-on-one matchup and 41-18 in a three-way contest including David Roth.

sources.name: Roll Call
sources.details: News coverage reported that Democratic nominee David Roth dropped out, leaving independent Todd Achilles as the main challenger to Republican incumbent Jim Risch, which changed the shape of the race but not the underlying GOP advantage.
